translations.text: An instruction delivered by our holy father, honored in every way, Apa Pachomius, the holy archimandrite, concerning a brother who had become angry with someone in the time of Apa Ebonh. He brought him to Tabennesi and spoke these words to him. Other elderly fathers were also there, rejoicing greatly in the peace of God.
May his holy blessing and the blessings of all the saints come upon us for the salvation of us all. Amen.
My son, listen and become wise, and accept the true teaching.
For there are two paths.
Either prove yourself worthy and obey God like Abraham, who left his land and committed himself to life as a stranger, living in tents with Isaac in the promised land as a foreigner.
He obeyed and humbled himself. He was brought into an inheritance until he was tested concerning Isaac.
He was strong in the trial and offered Isaac up as a sacrifice to God.
Because of this, God called him “my friend.”
Take for yourself also Jacob’s humility, his gentleness, and his endurance, until he became a light, seeing the Father of all, and was called Israel.
Take for yourself also Joseph’s wisdom and gentleness, and struggle with self-control and servitude until you become a king.
My son, emulate the lives of the saints and live according to their virtues.
Wake yourself up.
Do not be negligent.
Extinguish the worldly man in you, over whom you have stumbled.
Rise up; do not remain with the dead, so that Christ may shine upon you and grace may shine within you.
For it is patience that reveals all the gifts to you. The saints were patient and obtained the promises.
The boast of the saints is patience.
Be patient, so that you may be counted among the saints, believing that you will receive an imperishable crown.
A thought: bear it patiently until God gives you rest.
A fast: endure it with perseverance.
Prayer without hesitation in your private room, between you and God.
One heart with your brother.
Chastity in all your bodily members.
Chastity in your thoughts.
Purity of body and purity of heart.
A bowed neck and a humble heart.
Cheerfulness in times of anger.
If a thought weighs heavily on you, do not lose heart, but endure courageously, saying, “They have indeed surrounded me on every side.”
But I destroyed them in the name of the Lord.
Immediately God's help comes to you, and you cast them away from you. Gladness surrounds you, and the glory of God walks with you.
For gladness walks with the humble, and you will be satisfied as your soul desires.
For God's paths are humility of heart and gentleness.
For he said, “On whom will I look except the humble and the gentle?”
If you walk in the Lord’s ways, the Lord will watch over you and give you strength.
He will fill you with knowledge and wisdom, and the memory of you will remain before him at all times. He will rescue you from the devil and grant you his peace at your end.
My son, I command you to be watchful and sober, knowing those who lie in wait for you.
The spirit of cowardice and the spirit of unbelief go together.
The spirit of falsehood and the spirit of deceit go together.
The spirit of love of money, the spirit of trading, the spirit of swearing falsely, the spirit of wickedness, and evildoing go together.
The spirit of vanity and the spirit of arrogance go together.
The spirit of sexual immorality and impurity go together.
The spirit of hostility and the spirit of sorrow go together.
But woe to the miserable soul that they surround and rule over! In this way they cause it to become estranged from God,
because it has come under their authority, distracted this way and that until it reaches the depths of the underworld.
My son, listen to me; do not be neglectful.
Do not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids, so that you may escape like a gazelle from traps.
For all these spirits, my son, have troubled me many times since my childhood.
While I was in the desert, they would afflict me until my heart broke, so that I thought, “I do not have the strength to stand against the dragon’s threat.”
For he distresses me on every side.
If I come among other people, he sends them against me, and they fight against me.
If I withdraw into solitude, he afflicts me with his persistence.
My heart has grown numb within me countless times. I turn in every direction and find no rest.
But when I run to God with weeping, humility, fasting, and nights of watchfulness, the enemy grows weak before me, together with all his other spirits, and God’s courage comes to me.
And immediately I recognize God’s help, for through his acts of patience he teaches human beings about his power and his goodness.
My son, never envy anyone. Do not see someone being honored and say, “This person has already received his reward.”
Guard yourself against this thought, for it is very evil. God hates anyone who honors himself while hating his brother.
But the one who says of himself, “I am somebody,” when he is nothing, deceives himself. Who can help him?
He is proud, making his heart like the heart of God.

He says, “There is no one like me.” Now he will hear his rebuke: “You will go down to the underworld. They will throw you among the dead. They will spread maggots beneath you and cover you with worms.”
But the person who has acquired humility for himself has judged himself, saying,
“My sins are greater than everyone else’s.” He should judge no one and accuse no one. Who are you,
judging a servant who is not yours?
For the master of the one who has fallen has the power to set him on his feet.
Watch yourself, my son. Never reproach anyone.
Taste all the virtues and preserve them.
If you are a stranger, keep to yourself. Do not rush into people’s company or become involved in their affairs.
If you are poor, do not lose heart over anything, lest they reproach you, for poverty is an evil thing in the mouth of the ungodly. Have you not heard, “If you go hungry, you will grieve”?
And you will speak evil of the ruler and those with fatherly authority.

Take care also that they do not wage war against you over something you lack for your bodily needs, and that you do not lose heart over food. Instead, persevere: God is certainly already at work in secret.
Remember Habakkuk in Judea and Daniel in Chaldea.
For the distance between them amounts to forty-five stages, especially Daniel, at the bottom of the pit, as food for the wild beasts.
He prepared a meal for him.

Remember Elijah in the wilderness and the widow in Zarephath. The scourge of famine and the hardship of hunger weighed heavily on her, and she was in need, gathering firewood, but she did not lose heart.
Instead, she struggled and overcame. She obtained God’s promises, and her household enjoyed abundance during the famine.
Giving bread in a time of abundance is not strength, nor is it poverty if you lose heart in times of need.
For it is written about the saints: “They were in need, afflicted, and suffering.”
For they boast in their afflictions.
If you persevere in the struggle prescribed by the Scriptures, no slavery will come upon us, as it is written:
“Do not let anyone deceive you concerning eating and drinking, or the observance of a festival, a new moon, or a Sabbath. These are a shadow of the things to come.”
Meditate on God’s words at all times, persevere in hardship, and give thanks in everything.
Flee from human honor, and love the one who rebukes you in the fear of God.
Let everyone benefit you, so that you may benefit everyone. Persevere in your work and your good words.
Do not take a step forward and a step backward, lest God hate you.
For your crown will belong to those who persevere. And more and more, obey God so that he may save you.
When you sit among the brothers, do not put yourself forward with any foolish talk.
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego rejected Nebuchadnezzar’s deception. Therefore he could not draw them in with his musical instruments, nor could he deceive them with the food from his table.
Therefore they shattered his idol, which was forty-nine cubits high. They did not change with the one who changes.
Instead, they stood upright with the one who makes upright, namely God. Therefore he made them rulers over their enemies.
Daniel, too, did not obey the evil counsel of the Chaldeans. Therefore he became exceptionally distinguished.
And vigilance and wisdom were found in him. He shut the mouths of the wild lions.
Now then, my son, if you make God your hope, he will be your helper in your time of distress.
For anyone who approaches God must believe that he exists and that he will reward those who seek him.

These words were written for us so that we might believe in God and strive in matters small and great, with fasting, prayers, and the rest of our service—even down to a morsel that has dried in your mouth during a fast.
God will not forget it. Rather, you will find all these things precisely at the time of your distress.
Humble yourself in everything.
Hold back your words, even if you understand everything, in peace.
Do not consider yourself insulted, but bear every trial with joy. For if you knew the honor that follows trials,
you would not pray, “Take them away from me.” For it is better for you to pray, weep, and groan until you are saved than to lose heart and be taken captive.
O man, what are you doing in Babylon? You have grown old in a foreign land because you did not see fit to make God your own in uprightness.
Therefore, my brother, do not lose heart.
Perhaps you sometimes forget a little,
but your enemies neither sleep nor forget. Night and day they devise deceit against you.
Therefore do not pursue greatness, lest you be humbled and your enemies rejoice over you.
Instead, pursue humility, for whoever exalts himself will be humbled, but whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
If you cannot manage on your own, attach yourself to someone who lives according to the gospel of Christ, and you will advance with him.
Either obey or submit to someone who obeys. Either be strong and be called Elijah, or obey the strong and be called Elisha.
Because he obeyed Elijah, his spirit came upon him in double measure.
If you want to live among people, imitate Abraham, Lot, Moses, and Samuel.
If you want to live in the wilderness, look: all the prophets are before you.
Be like them, wandering in the deserts, the ravines, and the holes in the earth, destitute, afflicted, and suffering.
He also said, “The shade of the bricks and the spirit of the people who have suffered violence will bless you.”
Now the robber spoke a word on the cross. The Lord forgave his sins and took him into paradise.
How great is your honor if you endure a temptation, or a spirit of sexual immorality, or a spirit of pride, or any other passion!
Simply fight against the devil’s passions yourself, without following him.
And Jesus will graciously grant you what he has promised.
Guard yourself against forgetfulness, for it is the mother of all losses.
My son, flee from desire, for it darkens the mind.
It does not allow it to know the mystery of God.
And it makes you a stranger to the language of the Spirit.
And it does not allow you to carry the cross of Christ.
And it does not allow the heart to remain alert to the blessings of God.
Guard yourself against the desire to fill your belly, which makes you a stranger to the good things of paradise.
Guard yourself against defilement, which angers God and his angels.
My son, turn to God and love him. Flee from the enemy and hate him, so that God’s gifts may be yours and you may inherit the blessing of Judah, the son of Jacob.
For he said, “Judah, your brothers will bless you. Your hands will be on the necks of your enemies, and your father’s sons will serve you.”
Guard yourself against pride, for it is the beginning of every evil.
The beginning of pride is turning yourself away from God. What follows it is hardness of heart.
If you guard yourself against these things, your resting place is the heavenly Jerusalem.
If the Lord loves you and gives you honor,
guard yourself: do not become proud, but persevere in humility, so that you may remain in the honor God has given you.
Keep watch over yourself and remain alert, for blessed is the one who is found watchful, because he will be put in charge of his master’s possessions.
And he will enter the kingdom rejoicing, and the bridegroom’s friends will love him, because he was found watching over his vineyard.
My son, be patient in everything, for it is written, “Be diligent to present yourself as one approved by God, a worker who has no cause for shame.”
Press forward toward God like someone who sows and someone who reaps, and you will gather God’s good things into your storehouse.
Do not make a show like these hypocrites. Instead, renounce your heart’s desires and do God’s work, while working for your own salvation.

If a passion overwhelms you because of love of money, jealousy, hatred, or any other passion, be watchful. Take on the heart of a lion and a warrior's heart. Fight against them and destroy them as Sihon, Og, and all the kings of the Amorites were destroyed.
Then the beloved, only-begotten Son, King Jesus, will fight on your behalf, and you will inherit the cities of your enemies.
But cast every kind of pride away from you and be courageous.
See how, when Joshua son of Nun became courageous, God delivered his enemies into his hands.
If you become fainthearted, you become a stranger to God's law.
Faintheartedness fills you with excuses for cowardice, unbelief, and negligence, until you perish.
Have the heart of a lion, and cry out yourself, 'Who can separate us from the love of God?' And say, 'Even if my outer self is wasting away, my inner self is being renewed day by day.'
If you are in the desert, fight with prayers, fasting, and humility.
If you are among people, be wise as snakes and innocent as doves.
If someone insults you, bear it silently and put your hope in God, for he will act for your good.
But do not insult the image of God, for he is the one who said, 'Whoever honors me, I will honor; whoever dishonors me, I will dishonor.'
And if people honor you, do not rejoice, for it is written, 'Woe to you when everyone honors you.'
He also said, 'Blessed are you when people hate you, persecute you, and reject your name as evil.'
Consider also our fathers Barnabas and Paul: when people honored them, they tore their clothes and were distressed, hating the honor that comes from people.

Peter and John, for their part, when they were humiliated in the council, went out rejoicing because they had been considered worthy to be humiliated for the Lord's holy name, placing their hope in the honor of heaven.
But you, my son, flee from the comfort of this age so that you may enjoy yourself in the age to come.

Do not be negligent, letting day follow day, lest they come after you before you realize it, and you arrive at the [?] of your distress. Then those who change their faces will surround you, seize you boldly, and take you to their dark places, which are full of terror and distress.
Do not be distressed when people insult you. Instead, be distressed and sigh when you sin.
This is the true disgrace, and you sink under the wound of your sins.
I urge you most strongly to hate empty glory.
Vanity is the devil's weapon. This is how Eve was enslaved.
He said to her, 'Eat from the tree. Your eyes will open, and you will become like gods.'
She listened, thinking it was true, and pursued the glory of divinity.
Even her humanity was taken away from her.
You too, if you pursue empty glory, will find that it makes you a stranger to the glory of God.
But as for Eve, no one wrote to her to tell her about this battle before the devil tempted her.
For this reason, the Word of God came and took flesh from Mary the virgin, so that he might free Eve’s descendants.
But you have been taught about this battle through the saints who came before you, in the holy Scriptures.
Therefore, my brother, do not say, “I did not hear,” or “No one told me beforehand, yesterday or three days ago.”
For it is written, “Their voice has gone out over the whole earth, and their words have reached the ends of the inhabited world.”
Now, then, if people honor you, keep watch over your heart and give glory to God.
But if they insult you, give glory to God again, and thank him because you have been counted worthy to share the lot of his Son and his saints.
If they called your Lord “the deceiver,” and the prophets “those who revile him,” and others “madmen,” then how much more will they do so to us, who are earth and ashes?
Do not be distressed if they insult you. This is the path to your life.

But if it is your negligence that is dragging you along, then weep and mourn. For those brought up in scarlet have clothed themselves in dung because they neglected God’s law and followed the desires of their hearts.
Now, then, my son, weep before God at all times, for it is written, “Blessed is the one you have chosen and taken to yourself.”
You have placed thoughts in his heart for the valley of weeping, the place you established.
Cultivate innocence, and become like these innocent lambs, which endure being shorn without speaking.
Do not move from one place to another, saying, “I will find God in this place or that one.”
God said, “I fill heaven; I fill the earth.”
And again, “When you cross through water, I am with you, and the rivers will not drown you.”
Understand, my son, that God is within you, so that you may remain in the law and the commandments of God.
Look at the robber on the cross: he went to paradise.
Look also at Judas among the apostles: he betrayed his Lord.
Look at Rahab in her prostitution:
She was counted among the saints.
Look also at Eve in paradise: she was deceived.
Look at Job on the dung heap: he was compared to his Lord.
Look also at Adam in paradise: he fell away from the commandment.
Look at the angels of heaven: they were taken to the abyss.
Look also at Elijah and Enoch: they were taken to the kingdom of heaven. In every place, then, …
Seek God, and seek his face at all times.
Seek him as Abraham did: he obeyed God and offered up his son as a sacrifice to God.
He called him “my friend.”
Seek him as Joseph did, who struggled against defilement until he ruled over his enemies.
Seek him as Moses did, who followed his Lord.
He made him a lawgiver and showed him his form.
Daniel sought him, and he revealed great mysteries to him.
He rescued him from the mouths of the lions.
The three holy men sought him and found him in the fiery furnace.
Job ran to him, and he healed him of his affliction.
Susanna sought him, and he saved her from the hands of the lawless men.
Judith sought him earnestly and found him in the tent of Holofernes.
All these sought him, and he saved them. He saved others too.
You too, my son—how long will you remain negligent?
What is the basis for your negligence?
As it was last year, so it is this year.
As it was yesterday, so it is today.
How long will you remain negligent, with no progress being made by you?
Be watchful and awaken your heart.
For you must be brought to stand before God's judgment seat and give an account of what you have done in secret and what you have done openly.
If you go to a place where there is conflict, though it belongs to God, and the Spirit of God warns you,

saying, “Do not sleep in this place, for there is a trap in it,” and the devil, in turn, urges you, saying, “What happened to you the first time?” or, “Even if you see something, you will not be distressed,”

do not listen to his deceitful talk, lest the Spirit of God withdraw from you and you become weak and powerless like Samson, and the Philistines bind you and take you to the grinding place, which is the gnashing of teeth,
and you become a laughingstock to them—that is, they gloat over you—and you do not know the way to your city because they have gouged out your eyes,
because you revealed your heart to Delilah, that is, the devil, who captured you by deceit, because you abandoned the counsel of the Spirit.
You have also seen what this violent anger did to David, except that he quickly repented concerning Uriah’s wife.
It is also written: “You have seen my wrath; be afraid.”
Look, you have been told that he did not spare the saints.

Be watchful, then, and remember your vows. Flee this [?] and separate yourself from it, lest it gouge out the eyes of your mind and make you blind, so that you do not know the road to the city where you dwell.
Again: Know the city of Christ and give him glory, because he died for you.
Why, when a brother speaks a word against you, do you become angry and act like these wild beasts toward him?
Do you not remember that Christ died for you?
But when your enemy—that is, the devil—provokes you, you incline your ear to him, and he pours filth into it. You open your heart and swallow the poison he has cast to you.

You poor man, is this the time for you to become a wild beast? Or become like a fire until you burn up all his wickedness, tear open your heart, and release its stench of lawlessness, lest the poison strike you and you die.
Man, you did not put up with a small word that your brother said to you.
But your enemy is seeking to swallow your soul. What, then, have you done?
You have become indifferent toward him. No, my beloved! Do not let them reproach you by saying, “Instead of the gold ornament on the head, they will find baldness because of their deeds.”
Instead, stay alert, gladly bear with anyone who insults you, be patient with your brother, and do not fear bodily suffering.
My son, pay attention to the words of the wise Paul, as he says: “Chains and afflictions await me in Jerusalem.”
“But I do not value my life at all, so that I may finish my race.”
And: “I am ready to die in Jerusalem for the name of my Lord Jesus Christ.”
For neither suffering nor temptation prevented the saints from going to the Lord.
So steady yourself and be strong. What have you to do with the devil’s cowardice?
Instead, pursue the courage of the saints.
My son, why are you fleeing from Adonai, the Lord of hosts?
You, for your part, are running after the captivity of the Chaldeans.
Why do you set your heart on eating with the demons?
My son, guard yourself against sexual immorality.
Do not corrupt the members of Christ.
Do not obey the demons and make the members of Christ members of a prostitute.
Remember the anguish of the punishments.
Set God’s judgment before you and flee from every desire.
Strip yourself of the old person and his deeds, and put on the new person.
Remember the distress of the moment when you leave the body.
O my son, run to God, for he is the one who created you, and he endured these sufferings for your sake.
For he said, “I gave my back to whips and my cheeks to those who plucked out my beard. I did not turn my face away from shame and spitting.”
O man, what have you to do with the road to Egypt, that you should drink water from the turbid Gihon?
What have you to do with these troubled thoughts?
Wait until these sufferings come upon you.
Instead, turn back and weep over your sins.
For it is written, “If you make an offering for your sins, your souls will see offspring who live long.”
You see, then, O man, that transgression is evil, and that sin produces much suffering and distress.
O man, hurry! Flee from sin and remember the hour of death.
For it is written, “A wise person crushes sin,” and, “The faces of those who live ascetic lives will shine like the sun.”
Remember Moses too: he chose to suffer with the people of God rather than enjoy sin for a time.
If you love the sufferings of the saints, they will become your companions and intercede for you before God.
And he will grant you every good request, because you have taken up your cross and followed your Lord.
Do not pursue a seat of human honor, so that God will shelter you from the storm you do not know about and restore you to his capital city, the heavenly Jerusalem.
Also test everything.
Hold on to what is good. Likewise, do not mock the image of God.
Guard your youth too, so that you will safeguard your old age, lest you be ashamed and feel remorse in the valley of Jehoshaphat.
All of God's creation will look at you and reproach you, saying:
“Every day we thought you were a sheep, but here we have found you to be a wolf. Go now to the pit of the underworld. Cast yourself now into the heart of the earth.”

Oh, this great shame! A little while ago you were walking in the world, and people honored you as a chosen one. But when you came to the valley of Jehoshaphat, the place of judgment, they found you naked.
And everyone will see your sins and your shameful conduct, exposed before God and human beings.
Woe to you at that hour! Where will you turn your face?
Or what will you open your mouth and say? Your sins cling to your soul, which is black like charcoal.

What will you do at that hour? You will weep, but they will not accept your tears. You will plead, but they will not accept your pleas, because those into whose hands you have been delivered are merciless.
Oh, woe at the moment when you hear the terrifying voice that cuts you off: “Let sinners return to Hades.”
And again: “Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.”
And again: “I hated those who commit transgressions, so that I might wipe out from the Lord’s city all those who practice lawlessness.”
Now, then, my son, use this world with detachment, conducting yourself without self-importance.
Follow the Lord in everything, so that you may find confidence in the Valley of Jehoshaphat.
Let them also see you in the world as one of those rejected, but on the day of judgment let them find you clothed in glory.
Do not put your trust in any person for the comfort of your soul. Instead, cast your care upon the Lord, and he will sustain you.
Look at Elijah, who trusted in him beside the brook Cherith, where he sustained him through a raven.
Guard yourself very carefully against sexual immorality, for it has deceived many and cast them down.
Do not make friends with a young person.
Do not run toward a woman.
Flee bodily comfort, for companionship flares up like a fire.
Do not run toward any flesh, because when a stone strikes steel, fire flares up and burns a great deal of material.
Run toward the Lord at all times and sit beneath his shadow, for whoever dwells in the protection of the Most High will remain beneath the shadow of the God of heaven and will never be shaken.
Remember the Lord, and let the heavenly Jerusalem rise into your heart. You will live in heaven’s blessing, and the glory of God will carry you.
With every precaution, guard your body and your heart.
Pursue peace and purity, which are bound together, so that you may see God.
Do not be angry with anyone either, for whoever is angry with his brother is an enemy of God.
And whoever is at peace with his brother is at peace with God.

Now, then, you understand that nothing is greater than peace, so that each person should love his brother. Even if you are pure from every sin, if you are an enemy of your brother, you are a stranger to God.
For it is written: “Seek peace and purity, for they are bound together.”
And again it is written: “Even if I have all faith, so that I can move mountains, but have no love within me, I will gain nothing.”
Love builds up.
What will cleanse defilement? If there is hatred or hostility in your heart, where is your purity?

The Lord said through Jeremiah: “He speaks to his neighbor with peaceful words, but hostility is in his heart. He speaks deceitfully to his neighbor, while hostility is in his heart, or while he is thinking of hostility.”
“Will I not be angry over these things?” says the Lord.
“Or will my soul not take revenge on a nation like this?”
Thus he is saying that whoever is an enemy of his brother is the heathen, because the heathens walk in darkness and have not known the light.
This is how it is with someone who hates his brother: he walks in darkness and does not know God.
For the hatred of hostility has closed his eyes, and he does not see the image of God.
The Lord commands us: “Love your enemies. Bless those who curse you. Do good to those who persecute us.”

Then how great a danger we are in when we hate one another—our fellow members joined to us, the children of God, the branches of the true vine, the sheep of the spiritual flock whom the true shepherd, the only Son of God, gathered together when he offered himself as a sacrifice for us! This highly valued person, for whom the living Word endured these sufferings—you too hate him.
O man, why envy and empty glory?
Or love of money, or pride? These are the things through which the enemy has bound you, for he has made you a stranger to God.
What defense will you present to Christ? He will tell you, “To the extent that you hate your brother, it is me that you hate.”
But you will go into eternal punishment because [?] you are an enemy to your brother.
Your brother, however, will enter eternal life because he humbles himself before you for Jesus' sake.
Let us therefore seek the remedy for the wound before we die.
O my beloved, let us run to the gospel, the true law of Christ, who is God. And we will hear him saying, “Do not condemn, so that you will not be condemned.”
Forgive, so that you may be forgiven.
If you will not forgive, you too will not be forgiven.

If you harbor resentment against your brother, prepare yourself for punishments for your offenses, for your transgression, your acts of sexual immorality that you commit, thefts, your lies, your idle words, your evil thoughts, your greed, and your evil deeds, for which you will give an account at Christ’s judgment seat.
All God’s creation will be watching you, while all the angels and the entire heavenly army stand with their swords drawn, compelling you to present your defense and confess your sins.
With all your clothing [?], your mouth closed, and you speechless, with nothing to say, how much will you have to account for?
O wretched man, the many acts of sexual immorality that are [?] to your soul, the lusts of the eyes,
the evil thoughts that disturb the spirit and grieve the soul, the mouth’s downfall, the tongue that speaks empty words and defiles the whole body,
the fingers that make wicked gestures, the slanders, the envy, the hatred, the spite, the mockery directed against the image of God,

the condemnation, desires such as these that have deprived you of the good things of paradise, the passion for slander that speaks empty words against them, the evil thought directed against the image of God,
the anger, the strife, the shamelessness, the impudence, the malicious thinking of your heart, mercilessness, boasting—
you will be questioned about all these things because you harbored resentment against your brother and did not reconcile as you must, in the love of God.
Have you not heard that love covers a multitude of sins?
And that “This is what your Father in heaven will do to you: if you do not forgive one another from your heart, your Father in heaven will not forgive you your sins.”
Look, my beloved, you know that we have clothed ourselves with Christ, who is good and loves humanity.
Let us not allow ourselves to be deprived of it because of our evil deeds, since we have promised God purity and have vowed to live as monks.
Let us practice its works, which are these: fasting, unceasing prayer, purity of body, and purity of heart.
If we have promised God purity, let us not be found committing acts of sexual immorality of indescribable kinds.
For he said, “They committed sexual immorality in many ways.”
Brothers, do not let us be found doing such deeds and be found beneath everyone else.
We have also pledged ourselves to be disciples of Christ.
Let us endure hardship, because hardship reduces impurity.
Now, then, the contest is set before us. Let us not give up, so that we do not become slaves of sin.
We have been appointed to give light to the world. Do not let people stumble because of you. Let us maintain silence.
For many have been saved through this. Be sober, brothers.
Let us not call one another to account, so that we are not called to account at the time of punishment, whether you are virgins, renunciants, or hermits.
Nevertheless, he will say to us, “Repay what belongs to me, with its interest.” He will find fault with us and say to us, “Where is the wedding garment?”
“Where is the light of the lamps?”
“If you are my son, where is your fear of me?”
“If you hated me in this world, then depart from me, for I do not know you.”
“If you hated your brother, then you are a stranger to my kingdom.”

“If you held a grudge against your brother and did not forgive him, then your hands will be bound behind you, along with your feet, and you will be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
“If you struck your brother, then you will be handed over to merciless angels, and they will flog you with whips of fire forever.”
“You did not honor my image. You insulted me, mocked me, and put me to shame.”
“Because of this, I will not show you regard in the distress of your time of need.”
“You [?] did not make peace with your brother in this world.”
“I, in turn, will have nothing to do with you on the day of the great judgment.”
“You mocked the poor man; it is me you are insulting.”
“You struck the needy man; you too are the companion of the one who struck me in my humiliation on the cross.”
“Did I deprive you of anything during my stay in the world?”
“Did I not freely give you my body and my blood as food that gives life?”
“Did I not taste death for you to redeem you?”
“Did I not reveal to you the mystery of the heavens, to make you my brother and companion?”
“Did I not give you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy?”
“Did I not give you many life-giving remedies through which you would be saved?”
My mighty deeds, my signs, and my wonders, which I bore in the world as weapons of warfare, I gave to you so that you could arm yourself with them and strike down Goliath, who is the devil.
Now, what do you lack that would make you become a stranger to me?
It is your own negligence alone that has thrown you into the pit of the underworld.
Now then, my son, we will hear these things and greater things than these if we are negligent and do not heed the need to forgive one another.
Let us be watchful.
And let us recognize the virtues of God, which will help us on the day of death: these guides in the midst of the fierce and terrifying battle, these that raise the soul from the dead.
First, they gave us faith and knowledge so that we could cast out the unbelief within us.
After that, they gave us wisdom and understanding so that we could recognize the devil’s intention, flee from him, and hate him.
They proclaimed to us fasting, prayer, and self-control, which will bring restraint and calm to the body because of the passions.
They gave us purity and vigilance, because of which God will dwell within us.
We have been given patience and gentleness. If we preserve all these things, we will inherit the glory of God.
They gave us love and peace, these mighty ones in battle, for no enemy can enter the place where they are.
They instructed us about joy so that through it we could fight against sorrow.
They also taught us generosity and kindness.
They gave us holy prayer and perseverance, which fill the soul with light.
They gave us humility and discernment, which crush wickedness.
They wrote to us about not judging, so that we could overcome lying, that evil sore within a person.
For if we do not judge, we will not be judged on the day of judgment.
For they gave us endurance of suffering and acceptance of mistreatment, so that the desire for revenge would not rise up again.
For our fathers completed their lives in hunger, thirst, and many hardships, until they acquired purity for themselves.
Above all, they fled from wine drinking, which is full of every kind of harm.
These disturbances, these agitations, and these disorders are in our limbs because of excessive wine.
It is madness full of sins, the worm and caterpillar that devour the crops.
For the pleasure of never being satisfied makes thought foolish, makes the conscience shameless, and tears away the tongue’s bridle.
The safeguard for everything is not to grieve the Holy Spirit or become drunk with pleasure.
For he said, “The priest and the prophet became drunk because of wine.”
Wine is uncontrollable, and drunkenness is disgraceful. Whoever gives himself over to these will not be free from sin.
Wine is good if you drink it in moderation. If you fix your eyes on bowls and cups, you will walk about naked like a pestle.
Therefore, let everyone who has prepared to become a disciple of Jesus keep away from wine and drunkenness.
For our fathers knew how great the harm caused by wine would be, and they kept away from it. They drank only a little because of illness.

For if they allowed a little to the great worker Timothy, whose body suffered from many illnesses, then what about someone who seethes in the wickedness of the prime of youth, with defilements and passions abounding in him?
What shall I say to them? I am afraid to say, “Do not let him drink at all,” lest someone who hates his salvation grumble against me.
For these words are difficult for many people in this age.

Nevertheless, my beloved, it is good to be watchful, and hardship is beneficial. For whoever disciplines himself will bring his ship safely into the good and holy harbor of salvation, and he will be satisfied with the good things of heaven.
But greater than all these, we have also been given humility, which guards all the virtues. Humility is this great, holy power with which God clothed himself when he came into the world.
The wall of the virtues, the treasury of deeds, the saving weapon, the healer of every sorrow.
When they made these fine linens and these gold ornaments for the tabernacle, and all these decorations, they covered them with a covering of haircloth.
It is insignificant in the eyes of people, but it is choice and honored before God.
If we acquire it for ourselves, we will trample on all the power of the enemy.
For he said, “I will look upon no one except the humble and the contrite.”
Let us not lose heart in this time of wickedness, because boasting and human wisdom have increased.

Greed has increased. Sexual immorality has become king through the satisfaction of the flesh. Pride has taken power. The young have stopped obeying their elders, and the elders have given up caring for the young. Everyone has followed the desires of his own heart.
Now is the time for us to cry out with the prophet, “Woe to me, my soul! For the God-fearing person has perished from the earth.”
“And there was no upright person among humanity,” according to Christ—that is, there is none at all—and, “Everyone has oppressed his neighbor.”
Strive, my beloved, for the time has drawn near and the days have been shortened. There is no father teaching his children, and no child obeying his father.
The good virgins have disappeared. The holy fathers everywhere have fallen asleep. The mothers have disappeared like these widows. We have become like orphans.
They have trampled on the humble and brought oppression upon the homes of the poor.
Therefore, only a little time remains before God's wrath comes and we grieve with no one to comfort us.
All these things have happened to us because we have not disciplined ourselves.
Let us strive, my beloved, so that we may receive the crown that has been prepared.
The throne is set out. The door of the kingdom is open. “To the one who conquers, I will give some of the hidden manna.”
If we struggle and overcome the passions, we will reign forever. But if they overcome us, we will regret it and weep bitterly.
Let us fight against ourselves while repentance is still available to us.
Let us bear hardship so that we may be renewed in purity. Let us love people,
so that we may become friends of Jesus, who loves humanity.
If we have vowed to God to live as monks in love,
Not merely bodily virginity, but also virginity on your part, free from every sin.
For some virgins were turned away in the Gospel because of their laxity. Those who keep watch diligently enter the bridal chamber.
May everyone, then, enter that place forever.
The love of money, on account of which they fight against us.

If you want to acquire wealth for yourself—things that are soot and firebrands—through greed for more, or through trading, or through taking things by force, or through wrongdoing, or through so much manual work that you have no time to serve God—in any case, in whatever way,
if you have desired to accumulate gold or money for yourself, remember what he said in the Gospel: “Fool! Tonight they will take your soul from you. And whose will the things you have prepared be?”
Likewise: “He gathers things together without knowing for whom he gathers them.”
Struggle, my beloved, and resist the passions.

And you say, “I will do as Abraham did. I will reach up to God Most High, who created heaven and earth, declaring that I will take nothing from all that belongs to you, from a thread to a sandal strap.”

A humble stranger is a great blessing, and the Lord loves the convert, giving him bread and clothing. And concerning faintheartedness, on account of which they fight against us, saying, “Store things up because of [?] need,”
remember that it is written: “Your storehouses will be cursed, along with whatever is in them.”
Again, concerning gold and money, James said: “Their corrosion will testify against you, and the corrosion will consume your flesh like fire.”
And: “A righteous man who has no idol is preferable, as he looks at their [?].”
Purify yourself also from what is accursed before the Lord calls you. For you have placed your hope in God, because it is written: “Let your hearts be pure and wholly devoted to God.”
I greet you, my beloved in the Lord.
For you have made God your helper. You have become beloved to him, and you have set your heart on walking in God's commandments.
May God himself bless you, and may your spring become a river for you, and your river become a sea for them,
For you are a chariot, being a horseman of self-control, with the lamp of God burning above you as you shine with the hidden light of the Spirit.
as you manage your words with sound judgment,
God will grant you the sobriety of the saints, and no idol will be found in your city.
and plant your feet on the necks of the rulers of darkness,
and see the commander of the Lord's army standing at your right hand,
and drown Pharaoh and his multitude,
and bring your people across the salt sea, which is this life. Amen.
After these things, I again command you not to let down your guard. For this is the demons’ delight: that a person lets down his guard and they lead him into a trap before he realizes it.
So do not neglect to learn the fear of the Lord.
And make progress like young plants.
And you will please God like a young calf tossing its horns at the manger.
Also be a person who is strong in deed and word.
Do not put on a show like the hypocrites, lest your portion be assigned with theirs.
Do not waste a single day of your life. Consider what you will give to God each and every day.
Sit by yourself like a wise governor and judge your thoughts, whether you are living in solitude or among others.
In any case, judge yourself every day.
For it is better to be among a thousand people in complete humility than to be alone in a hyena’s den, living in pride.
They testified about Lot, while he was in Sodom, that he was a good and faithful man.
But we have also heard about Cain that there was no one on earth with him except three other people, yet he became wicked.
Now, then, the struggle is set before you. Examine what comes upon you every day, to see whether you are counted among us or among those who fight against us.
The demons do not come to you only from the right; the left is obvious to everyone.
For truly, they also fought against me from the right. They brought me the devil bound like a mountain goat, but the Lord helped me.
I did not fear them, nor did I let down my guard with them.
And many times they [?] us through deeds of the devil from the right. And he rushed at me. He also dared to tempt the Lord, but the Lord defeated him and his tricks.
Now, then, my son, clothe yourself in humility and take Christ and his good Father as your advisers.
And become the companion of a man of God, in whose heart is the law of God.
And make yourself like a poor man carrying his cross, a companion of weeping.
And make yourself poor as well, with a cloth on your head. Let your dwelling become a tomb for you until God raises you up and gives you the crown of victory.
If you ever quarrel with a brother who troubles you with something he says,
or your heart burns against a brother, and you say, “He does not deserve these things,”
or the enemy works in you against someone, saying, “He does not deserve these honors,” and you accept the statement,
or a thought from the devil comes, and the battle in your mind grows stronger,
and you become entangled with your brother, you know that there is no balm in Gilead and no physician around you.
Now turn your attention to quietness and consciousness of God.
Weep alone with Christ, and the Spirit of Jesus will speak with you in your thoughts.
He will rebuke you concerning the commandment: “There is no need for you to struggle alone, making yourself like a wild beast, as though this poison were inside you.”
Remember that you too have fallen many times.
Have you not heard Christ saying, “Forgive your brother seventy-seven times”?
Do you not yourself often weep and plead, “Forgive me for the multitude of my sins”?
Yet now you hold on to the little that your brother owes.
Immediately the Spirit of God brings judgment before you, along with the fear of punishment.
You remember the saints, that they were considered worthy of being insulted.
And you remember Christ, that they insulted him.
They spat on him and mocked him for your sake.
Immediately he fills your heart with compassion and fear, and you fall on your face, weeping and saying, “Forgive me, my Lord, for I have caused suffering to your image.”
Immediately you rise in the comfort of repentance.
You run to your brother.
Your heart is relieved.
Your face is cheerful, and your mouth is full of joy.
Peace surrounds you as you smile and reach out to your brother, saying, “Forgive me, my brother, for I have caused you suffering.”
Your weeping increases, and great joy comes from the weeping.
Peace rejoices among you, and the Spirit of God also rejoices and cries out, saying, “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they are the ones who will be called children of God.”
When the enemy hears the sound of this proclamation, he is put to shame.
God receives glory, and a great blessing comes to you.
Now then, my brother, let us struggle against ourselves. You know that stumbling has occurred everywhere.
The churches are filled with quarrelsome and angry people.
The communities of monks have become lovers of greatness. Pride has become king.
No one offers encouragement to his neighbor. Instead, each one torments his neighbor.
We have fallen into the midst of these hardships.
There is neither a prophet nor a person with spiritual knowledge.
No one rebukes anyone, because hard-heartedness has increased.
But the person who understands will remain silent, because it is an evil time.
Each one has made himself king on his own. They despise what is proper.
Now, then, my brother, make peace with your brother, and pray for me
too, because I cannot do any work, but I am afflicted because of my desires.
But you, stay sober in everything.

Endure hardship. Do the work of an evangelist. Persevere through temptation. Complete the struggle of the monastic life, remaining humble and joyful, trembling before the words you have heard, and preserving your virginity.
And guard yourself against excess [?] and these foreign voices [?].
Do not be outside the writings of the saints, but remain firm in faith in Christ Jesus our Lord. Through him, glory be to him and his good Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. [?] Amen.
Bless us.
Through the diligence and care of our God-loving brother Michael, the son of the blessed Stephen, the farmer from Moui, a native of the plain north of the city of Esna.
He had this book made through his own labor.

He donated it to the monastery of Saint Mercurius on the mountain of the city of Edfu, for the salvation of his soul, so that it might be read in the name of Saint John and the holy Apa Pachomius, and so that Saint Mercurius, the commander and mighty martyr, together with Saint John the Baptist and forerunner of Christ and Saint Apa Pachomius the archimandrite, might plead with Christ on his behalf.

May he bless him in this world and save him from all the snares of the devil and evil people, and help him in every undertaking for good [?]. And after the end of this life, may he be worthy of forgiveness for his sins and receive an inheritance with all the saints. So be it. Amen.
Remember me too, Theopistus, the lowly [?] deacon, the son of Severus, the archpriest of Saint Mercurius in the city of Esna.
I wrote this book with my own hand. Pray for me, that God may forgive me the multitude of my sins, for they are very many. So be it.
Written in the month of [?], on the sixteenth, in the fifteenth indiction, in year 701 of the holy martyrs, while [?] Abba Nicodemus [?] of the city of Apollonopolis [?].
